description: Matched-CV audit studies consistently find callback gaps by name across many labour markets. The Mexican version runs through both the surname and any indication of where schooling happened.
energy_note: Identical CV, different surname, fewer calls.

aspect: Arceo-Gómez and Campos-Vázquez did it inside Mexico
description: Their correspondence work on race and appearance in the Mexican labour market, and on discrimination in job advertisements and callbacks, found the sorting happens domestically too - it is not only a border phenomenon.
energy_note: The same filter operates at home.

aspect: Qualifications are discounted across the line
description: A Mexican degree or trade certification is frequently treated as unverifiable abroad, pushing trained men into unskilled work and keeping them there.

aspect: SCENE - the name on the application
description: He applies as Jose Ramirez Delgado. Nothing. A friend suggests he try 'Joe Ramirez'. He gets two callbacks in a fortnight for the same kind of role. He does not tell anyone he did this, including his father, who chose the name.
energy_note: Two callbacks, and something he will not mention to his father.
